@about: Open solver cases add-on for PartCraft (suggestion 1309). Keys p.* are the problem list (codes of lib/opensolvers).
name: Open solver cases
cmd.export: Open solver cases: export the case
panel.honest: Set a study up here, export a ready-to-run case folder for an outside solver, run it on your own computer, then bring the results back. The solvers are separate programs that you add yourself. No case from this add-on has yet been run in the real solvers: check a case before you rely on it.
h.need: What you need on your computer
target.label: Kind of case
flow.internal: Inside: the model is the fluid space
flow.side: Box to the sides (× model size)
flow.external_note: The model is a body in a box of fluid. The box faces are the inlet, the outlet and slip sides; the model's faces are walls. In PartCraft Y is up.
flow.internal_note: Model the fluid space itself as a solid (the inside of the duct, not its walls). Pick its inlet and outlet faces; faces you do not pick are walls.
structure.note: Written for {v}: a command file, the mesh as text and a run file. Linear elastic, one material.
impact.note: Written for {v}: a starter deck and an engine deck. The Johnson-Cook numbers are yours to type; none are preset.
faces.external_note: A named wall is optional: it gives those faces their own patch, so their force can be read on its own.
mat.label: Material
export.units_flow: Units in the files: metres, kilograms, seconds; the model's millimetres are written × 0.001. Pressure is kinematic (pressure ÷ density).
export.units_structure: Units in the files: mm, tonne, s (so N and MPa). Density is written in t/mm³ (kg/m³ × 1e-12). Heat: mm, W, °C.
export.units_impact: Units in the files: tonne (Mg), mm, s (so N and MPa). Speeds are written in mm/s, density in t/mm³.
results.how_flow: After the run, convert with foamToVTK in ASCII (the README gives the command) and choose the .vtk files of the wall patches, and the forces text file.
results.how_structure: After the run, choose the .resu file. Keep the element size as it was when the case was written.
results.how_impact: After the run, convert each animation file with the solver's own anim_to_vtk tool (the README gives the command) and choose the .vtk files.
plot.none: There is nothing to plot yet: import results first.
plot.shown: Plot placed on the model ({n} colour bands, {tris} triangles, deformation ×{scale}). Blue is the lowest value, red the highest.
plot.shown_thinned: Plot placed on the model ({n} colour bands, deformation ×{scale}). The surface was thinned to {tris} triangles to fit the display. Blue is the lowest value, red the highest.
plot.range: {name}: {lo} to {hi}, in the file's own units.
forces.title: Force at time {t}
forces.note: The last of {n} rows of the forces file, in newtons, in the case's axes.
need.separate: These programs are separate from CadCraft. They are not part of it, and you add them to your own computer yourself. CadCraft only writes text files for them and reads the text files they write.
need.for_structure: For stress, frequency and heat studies.
need.never: CadCraft cannot start a program on your computer: you run the solver yourself with the commands in the README of each case.
msg.pick: Click faces of the part in the 3D view to add them to {id}, click again to take one off. Press Done picking when finished.
msg.no_faces: This part has no named faces to pick (use the mesh kernel or the exact kernel).
msg.max_faces: At most 64 faces on one item.
msg.no_part: There is no solid part yet. Build the part first.
msg.too_fine: An element size that small would make about {n} elements; the limit here is {max}. Use a larger size.
msg.stale: The part changed. Mesh and export again.
msg.copy_none: This part has no Simulation study or Solid FEM settings with fixtures or loads to copy.
msg.written: {name} written: {n} files. Unzip it, then follow its README.
msg.read: Read {n} result frames and {forces} force files.
undo.copy: Solver cases: copy from the study
undo.show: Solver cases: plot on the model
note.unrun: No case from this add-on has yet been run in the real solvers.
note.liability: An analysis aid, not a design approval; your engineer reviews the results.
p.group_empty: {id} has no faces on the model. Pick its faces again.
p.faces_gone: {id}: some of its faces are no longer in the part and were left out.
p.many_cells: The background mesh alone has {n} cells. Use a larger cell or smaller margins.
p.no_inlet: An internal flow needs an inlet. Add one and pick its faces.
p.no_outlet: An internal flow needs an outlet. Add one and pick its faces.
p.no_location: No point inside the fluid could be found for the mesher. Check that the model is a closed solid.
p.inlet_not_flat: {id} is not flat: the inlet velocity is written along its mean normal. Check it.
p.bad_elements: {n} elements have no volume. Mesh again with a different element size.
p.no_fixed: Nothing holds the part. Add fixed faces.
p.modal_free: Nothing holds the part: the first six frequencies will be zero (free body).
p.no_load: There is no load. Add a force, a pressure or own weight.
p.no_conductivity: A heat study needs the thermal conductivity. Type it under Material.
p.no_thermal: A heat study needs at least one temperature or convection face.
p.no_motion: Nothing moves: give a starting speed, pushed faces or gravity.
p.many_cycles: About {n} time steps: a long run. Shorten the run time or use a larger element size.
